config_locations.path: Settings > Tools > AI Assistant > Providers & API keys > Third-party AI providers (Beta)

requires_parent_login_for_byok.note: The OpenAI-compatible provider works without a JetBrains account or JetBrains AI subscription. Activate JetBrains AI and Start Free Trial are optional.

can_disable_login_prompt.how: No sign-in is needed for the OpenAI-compatible provider; skip Activate JetBrains AI. First start shows a User Agreement and a Data Sharing dialog (choose Don't Send). Choosing a third-party provider shows a Data Sharing with Third-Party AI Service Providers confirmation, which may appear more than once.

telemetry_controls.effect: Declines anonymous usage statistics; applies to all installed JetBrains products

telemetry_controls.where: confirmation shown when a third-party provider is chosen
telemetry_controls.effect: Confirms data may be sent to the hosts in the provider settings; JetBrains disclaims responsibility; may appear more than once
Optional; activating it alongside BYOK lets JetBrains AI cover features custom models do not support

telemetry_controls.setting: AI Assistant telemetry, error reporting, offline mode
telemetry_controls.effect: No setting documented for the provider

auth.native_helper_command_evidence: observed (no such field in the provider form)
auth.notes: The form has no custom header setting and no token command. Point the provider URL at the local token proxy (Appendix B of the guide); the API key field can hold any non-empty value because the proxy replaces it with a fresh JWT; the helper command that supplies the token is Appendix A of the guide. With a plain-HTTP proxy that speaks HTTP/1.1, select HTTP/1.1 (HTTP/2 cleartext was not tried).

api_format_notes: Chat uses the OpenAI Chat Completions API with stream true and Accept application/json,text/event-stream. The Responses API was not used in the chat path.
url_rule: The plugin appends only the endpoint name to the URL entered and does not add /v1. URL http://<host>/<prefix> gives GET <url>/models; URL http://<host>/<prefix>/v1 gives GET <url>/models and POST <url>/chat/completions (.../v1/models, .../v1/chat/completions). The URL must include /v1 or whatever prefix the gateway uses.
model_discovery_endpoint_behaviour: GET <url>/models, expecting the OpenAI list shape {"object":"list","data":[{"id":"<model-id>"}]}. Test Connection issues it twice. The Model Assignment dropdowns list the models returned by this call, shown as OpenAIAPI/<model-id>.
model_assignment_notes: After Test Connection reports Connected, chat answers 'No compatible model is available for Chat mode' until Core features and Instant helpers are set under Model Assignment to a model from the gateway list.
requests_per_prompt_notes: One chat prompt produced about 12 POSTs to <url>/chat/completions: one chat call with 35 tool definitions and about eleven background helper calls without tools (titles, summaries).

config_snippets.content:
Settings > Tools > AI Assistant > Providers & API keys > Third-party AI providers (Beta) > OpenAI-compatible
URL: http://127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>/<apim-api-path>/v1
API Key: <any-non-empty-placeholder>
HTTP version: HTTP/1.1 for a plain-HTTP proxy that speaks HTTP/1.1 (HTTP/2 is the default)
Tool calling: leave ticked if the model supports it
Then: Test Connection (reports Connected), and under Model Assignment set Core features and Instant helpers to the listed model

# Prints ONLY the raw JWT to stdout; on any problem prints a one-line reason to stderr and exits 1.
# Failing fast matters: both Claude Code and Codex retry hard on a bad token.
$Scope       = 'api://<apim-app-id>/.default'
$ExpectedAud = @('api://<apim-app-id>', '<apim-app-client-id>')   # accept both token forms
$MinLifeSecs = 60

$lines = & az account get-access-token --scope $Scope --query accessToken -o tsv 2>$null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine("get-apim-token: az failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE). Run: az login"); exit 1 }

# Tolerate banners/warnings on stdout: keep only the line that looks like a JWT.
$jwt = $lines | ForEach-Object { "$_".Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^eyJ[\w-]+\.[\w-]+\.[\w-]+$' } | Select-Object -Last 1
if (-not $jwt) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine('get-apim-token: az output contained no JWT'); exit 1 }

# Sanity-check the claims so a wrong audience or nearly-expired token fails here, not as an endless 401 loop.
$p = $jwt.Split('.')[1].Replace('-', '+').Replace('_', '/')
while ($p.Length % 4) { $p += '=' }
$claims = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($p)) | ConvertFrom-Json
$now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
if ($ExpectedAud -notcontains $claims.aud) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine("get-apim-token: token aud is '$($claims.aud)', expected '$($ExpectedAud -join "' or '")'"); exit 1 }
if ($claims.exp - $now -lt $MinLifeSecs) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine("get-apim-token: token expires in $($claims.exp - $now)s"); exit 1 }

[Console]::Out.Write($jwt)

"""Local token-injecting reverse proxy for tools that can only send a static key (VS Code Copilot BYOK, JetBrains, ...).

Clients send any dummy key to http://127.0.0.1:<port>; the proxy replaces Authorization with a fresh JWT obtained from a
helper command, streams the response back, and retries once on an upstream 401 with a forced token refresh.

usage: proxy.py --upstream https://<apim>.azure-api.net [--port 18081] [--margin-s 300] [--local-key K] -- <helper cmd...>
"""
import argparse
import asyncio
import base64
import json
import sys
import time

from aiohttp import ClientSession, ClientTimeout, web

HOP = {"connection", "keep-alive", "proxy-authenticate", "proxy-authorization", "te", "trailers",
       "transfer-encoding", "upgrade", "host", "content-length"}
DROP_IN = {"authorization", "x-api-key", "api-key"}


class TokenSource:
    def __init__(self, cmd, margin):
        self.cmd, self.margin, self.tok, self.exp, self.lock, self.fetches = cmd, margin, None, 0, asyncio.Lock(), 0

    async def get(self, force=False):
        async with self.lock:
            if not force and self.tok and self.exp - time.time() > self.margin:
                return self.tok
            p = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*self.cmd, stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE)
            out, err = await asyncio.wait_for(p.communicate(), 30)
            if p.returncode != 0:
                raise RuntimeError(err.decode(errors="replace").strip() or f"helper exited {p.returncode}")
            tok = out.decode().strip()
            seg = tok.split(".")[1]
            claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(seg + "=" * (-len(seg) % 4)))
            self.tok, self.exp, self.fetches = tok, claims["exp"], self.fetches + 1
            return tok


def make_app(upstream, tokens, local_key):
    async def handler(request):
        if request.path == "/_proxy/health":
            return web.json_response({"ok": True, "token_fetches": tokens.fetches})
        if local_key:
            sent = request.headers.get("x-api-key") or request.headers.get("api-key") or \
                   request.headers.get("Authorization", "").removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
            if sent != local_key:
                return web.json_response({"error": "bad local key"}, status=401)
        body = await request.read()
        fwd = {k: v for k, v in request.headers.items() if k.lower() not in HOP | DROP_IN}
        url = upstream.rstrip("/") + request.path_qs
        sess = request.app["sess"]
        for attempt in (0, 1):
            try:
                tok = await tokens.get(force=attempt == 1)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                return web.json_response({"error": "token helper failed", "detail": str(e)}, status=502)
            async with sess.request(request.method, url, data=body or None,
                                    headers={**fwd, "Authorization": f"Bearer {tok}"}, allow_redirects=False) as up:
                if up.status == 401 and attempt == 0:
                    continue
                resp = web.StreamResponse(status=up.status,
                                          headers={k: v for k, v in up.headers.items() if k.lower() not in HOP})
                await resp.prepare(request)
                async for chunk in up.content.iter_any():
                    await resp.write(chunk)
                await resp.write_eof()
                return resp

    async def on_start(app):
        app["sess"] = ClientSession(auto_decompress=False, timeout=ClientTimeout(total=None, sock_connect=15))

    async def on_stop(app):
        await app["sess"].close()

    app = web.Application(client_max_size=64 * 1024 * 1024)
    app.on_startup.append(on_start)
    app.on_cleanup.append(on_stop)
    app.router.add_route("*", "/{tail:.*}", handler)
    return app


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--upstream", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18081)
    ap.add_argument("--margin-s", type=int, default=300)
    ap.add_argument("--local-key")
    ap.add_argument("helper", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cmd = [x for x in a.helper if x != "--"]
    web.run_app(make_app(a.upstream, TokenSource(cmd, a.margin_s), a.local_key), host="127.0.0.1", port=a.port, print=lambda *_: None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

hosts_default.purpose: idle IDE at the welcome screen with the plugin installed and no provider configured made no external connections; default JetBrains cloud behaviour with no provider was not measured further

hosts_after_config.purpose: idle IDE and IDE during chat made no external connections; a local child process embeddings-server.exe starts

limits: About twelve model calls per chat prompt (one chat call with 35 tool definitions plus about eleven background calls without tools)
A model must be assigned under Model Assignment before chat works; OpenAI-compatible models are not assigned automatically
The gateway must serve the Chat Completions API with streaming and an OpenAI-shaped /models list; the Responses API is not used for chat
The URL must include /v1 or the gateway prefix; the plugin does not add it
No custom HTTP headers and no token command, so the token proxy is required for Entra tokens
HTTP/2 is the default; a plain-HTTP/1.1 proxy needs HTTP/1.1 selected; HTTP/2 cleartext not tried
Code completion uses JetBrains models unless the AI Completion section is configured separately
Agents cannot use local models; AI Assistant cannot call MCP tools with local models
BYOK usage is billed by the provider, not JetBrains AI credits
Administrators using IDE Services or JetBrains Central can set the provider or disable custom models
